subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WebSocket origin gate reusing checkBrowserOrigin

question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` become a pre-upgrade requirement for every Origin-bearing WebSocket client, or remain limited to the current browser/control-UI and webchat policy scope?
rationale: The protocol client type that currently controls enforcement is known only after the WebSocket upgrade, so choosing unconditional pre-upgrade enforcement changes a security and compatibility boundary that code review cannot safely infer.

options.title: Preserve client-aware scope
options.body: Keep the existing post-handshake client-aware policy and only add a pre-upgrade gate if an equivalent safe browser-only discriminator is available.

options.title: Approve broader origin enforcement
options.body: Intentionally apply the policy to all Origin-bearing clients, document the compatibility change, and add regression coverage plus current-head proof for native/custom-scheme and proxy scenarios.

recommendation.title: Preserve client-aware scope
recommendation.body: Keep the existing post-handshake client-aware policy and only add a pre-upgrade gate if an equivalent safe browser-only discriminator is available.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent released work on gateway browser-origin enforcement makes this the strongest available adjacent routing signal.
